report.title: City of San José 2025 Water Quality Report (San José Municipal Water System)

sources_described: Evergreen receives treated surface water purchased from Valley Water (imported water from the South Bay Aqueduct, Dyer Reservoir, Lake Del Valle and San Luis Reservoir plus local Anderson and Calero reservoirs, treated at three Valley Water plants in San José using ozone), supplemented during 2025 with groundwater from local deep-water wells; the Edenvale and Coyote Valley service areas are supplied 100 percent by groundwater from deep-water wells.

extraction_notes: Single 2025 report for the whole San José Municipal Water System (PWSIDs CA4310019 North San José/Alviso and CA4310020 Evergreen/Edenvale/Coyote Valley); the same PDF is saved under both reports/ directories and this JSON contains only the columns for this PWSID. The one data table is on PDF page 5 (printed as the back inside panel of the brochure) with six source columns, each with Average and Range sub-columns: 'Evergreen (Valley Water Treated Water)', 'Evergreen (Groundwater)', 'Edenvale* (Groundwater)', 'Coyote Valley** (Groundwater)', 'North San José/Alviso (SFPUC Treated Water)', 'North San José/Alviso (Groundwater)'; source_group = column name (asterisks dropped; they refer to the temporary-chlorination footnotes). Cells printed NA (not applicable) have no entry. Lead and Copper are printed once across the Evergreen/Edenvale/Coyote Valley columns and once across the North San José/Alviso columns (90th percentile, number of samples exceeding AL, 2024 customer-tap data). Sample year is 2025 (table titled '2025 Water Quality Data') except footnote a cells (superscript a = distribution system data in 2023) and footnote e lead/copper (2024). Where the Average cell is ND but the Range has a numeric high, value = range high (value_basis 'range_high', average null). MCL/PHG strings are copied as printed including '(4)'/'[4]' (MRDL/MRDLG), '[15]'/'[1300]' (AL) and '(0)' (MCLG). Total Coliform has a blank unit cell and 'Highest %'/'Range' sub-headers; recorded as % with value = highest monthly %. Turbidity appears three times: 'Turbidity (unfiltered sources)' and 'Turbidity (filtered sources)' in the Clarity section (printed as 'Highest Level = x') and a secondary-standard 'Turbidity' row. Anomalies copied as printed: Iron row unit 'ppm' with SMCL 0.3 but SFPUC values 18 / ND - 36 (almost certainly ppb); Potassium North San José/Alviso (Groundwater) average '16' with range 1.4 - 1.8. The report has no violations section; its only compliance statements are 'a reliable water supply that meets or exceeds all drinking water health standards' (p.6) and footnote d 'All filtered water sources met this standard'. Typical-source codes (last column) were not transcribed. This file holds the Evergreen (Valley Water Treated Water), Evergreen (Groundwater), Edenvale (Groundwater) and Coyote Valley (Groundwater) columns and the Evergreen/Edenvale/Coyote Valley lead and copper cells. Chloramine in Edenvale and Coyote Valley is printed 'NA' / 'NA - 3.2*' and 'NA - 3.8**' (temporary chlorination in May and November 2025 only); recorded as range high with a null average.
